title: A Streak Over the Lookout, Watched From the Telescope

content.question: Do the bright streaks that cross the sky at dusk come from the same direction each night, or do they scatter across the whole sky like loose thread?
content.method: At dusk I sat on the telescope, which is mine, and kept my eyes on the sky above the lookout rock for as long as the light allowed. I counted each streak, noted where it began and where it ended against the edge of the rock, and did not move until the stars came out properly. I did this in one sitting, with my tail wrapped over my paws so the wind would not disturb the count.
content.result: Three streaks crossed while I watched, and all three began from the same notch in the sky above the rock and ran down toward the sea. They were quick and left nothing behind but a faint line I could still see for a moment. I cannot say what they are made of, but they keep to one path, which is more than most things on this island manage. I will watch the same notch again tomorrow to see whether it is a habit of the sky or only a coincidence.
